summary: Initial Serenity Layer 1A decomposition of the broad Technology theme. The strongest decomposition is not by end-market ticker, but by physical and workflow chokepoints created by AI compute buildout: memory bandwidth, advanced packaging, optical interconnect, compound-semiconductor substrates/tools, semiconductor manufacturing data orchestration, data-center power/cooling, cybersecurity/automation control layers, and cloud/AI software deployment infrastructure. This Layer 1A intentionally avoids centering mega-cap AI leaders and instead maps six supply-chain nodes where underfollowed small/mid-cap or obscure suppliers may appear one or two steps away from obvious beneficiaries. No buy/sell conclusions are made.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The chokepoint may not only be HBM wafer capacity; it may also be backend packaging/test allocation and overflow capacity created by the crowding-out effect from AI memory demand.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prioritize USD 300M-10B Asia-listed and US-listed OSAT/test suppliers; include larger names only if the AI/HBM backend exposure is unusually pure and verifiable.
supply_chain_nodes.node: HBM-adjacent backend packaging, test, and OSAT overflow
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Screen OSATs, memory backend specialists, advanced test handlers, burn-in/test sockets, and panel-level packaging suppliers. Look for customer validation by AI chip vendors, utilization increases, pricing power, capex expansion, and revenue mix shifts toward memory or HPC packaging.

supply_chain_nodes.underfollowed_angle: These companies can be labeled as old-line OSAT or memory backend vendors rather than AI infrastructure winners, which may lower analyst attention despite exposure to HBM-driven capacity reallocation.
supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: AI accelerators require high-bandwidth memory and advanced backend capacity. If HBM producers prioritize scarce cleanroom, equipment, and capital toward HBM, conventional DRAM/NAND backend work may be pushed to third-party packaging and test providers, creating second-order beneficiaries outside the obvious HBM producers.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Large AI clusters require high-speed optical connectivity. The supply chain extends from switches and transceivers down to lasers, indium phosphide substrates, epitaxial growth, and the equipment used to add capacity.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The overlooked constraint may be not only physical capacity, but the software/data layer that coordinates yield ramp, production visibility, and secure collaboration across manufacturing tiers.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer USD 300M-5B software companies with semiconductor-specific revenue, high gross margins, recurring revenue, and customer concentration that can be traced to leading fabs, OSATs, or equipment vendors.

Verify whether customers use the platform for high-volume manufacturing, equipment connectivity, yield ramp, and supply-chain coordination rather than generic analytics.

As manufacturing complexity rises, secure data sharing, yield analytics, equipment connectivity, and process orchestration can become non-obvious software bottlenecks.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: As AI data-center deployment scales, the limiting factors may shift from server availability to site-level power, cooling, electrical gear, and qualified installers/components.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Target USD 300M-10B industrial suppliers with growing data-center revenue disclosures; include private-customer dependency and backlog conversion as key verification points.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Use a two-lane funnel. Lane 1 maps reference leaders only as demand validators: NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, TSMC, ASML, Arista, Vertiv, Eaton, Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta. Lane 2 searches for public companies one or two steps removed from those leaders: OSAT overflow beneficiaries, memory backend test providers, panel-level packaging suppliers, InP substrate suppliers, epitaxy toolmakers, optical component/toolchain suppliers, semiconductor manufacturing data platforms, power/cooling component vendors, and niche cybersecurity/automation software providers. Prefer USD 300M-10B market-cap candidates where plausible; allow USD 10B-30B only for unusually pure exposure; treat micro-caps as speculative shadow candidates requiring stronger verification.
supply_side_constraints: HBM producer capacity and downstream advanced packaging/test capacity may be constrained through 2027 based on supplied search context
OSAT and backend memory/test capacity may be crowded out as IDMs prioritize higher-margin HBM, creating overflow demand for third-party packaging/test providers
Optical connectivity supply may face constraints at several layers: lasers, indium phosphide substrates, epitaxy capacity, silicon photonics foundry capacity, transceiver assembly, and epitaxy tools
Compound-semiconductor substrate supply appears concentrated in a small number of suppliers based on supplied search context
Semiconductor data interoperability and secure manufacturing coordination may become a workflow bottleneck as production spans fabless, foundry, OSAT, test, and equipment vendors
